query: How can a relational database be made to answer lookups faster?
note: Shares almost no vocabulary with db-index-001 ('B-tree index', 'read time'). The canonical case for vector search over lexical.

query: write-ahead log durability fsync
note: Three exact concept keys of db-tx-002. Lexical search should win outright.

query: MVCC
note: Known gap: db-conc-003 is the MVCC question but the acronym appears nowhere in its text or concepts (the key is multiversion_concurrency_control). Lexical cannot match an absent string; vector has little to work with. Kept deliberately so the evaluation records a real failure.

query: Two people edited at the same time and the invariant broke even though both checks passed
note: Describes write skew without naming it. db-iso-002 is the write-skew question; lost update and deadlock are neighbouring concurrency failures.

query: deadlock detection lock ordering
note: Two exact concept keys of db-conc-002 and nothing else in the bank competes.

query: My endpoint issues one extra database call for every row it renders
note: The N+1 problem stated as a symptom rather than by name.

query: ACID atomicity
note: Exact terms from db-tx-001's text and concepts.

query: Users cannot see a record they just saved when the page reloads
note: Almost a paraphrase of db-repl-001's scenario; tests read-your-writes recall.

query: third normal form update anomaly
note: Exact concept keys of db-norm-001 (lexical) and a topically adjacent denormalisation question (vector).

query: How do I model a relationship that itself carries extra attributes?
note: db-model-002 is the enrolment/junction-table question; the query never says 'many-to-many' or 'junction'.

query: Does the order of columns in a multi-column index matter?
note: Three indexing questions are all plausible candidates; only db-index-002 is about column order. A ranking test, not a recall test.

query: A table has billions of rows and every query filters on a date range
note: Close paraphrase of db-part-001's scenario.

query: LEFT JOIN WHERE clause turns into inner join
note: Exact phrasing from db-joins-001.

query: Should an email address be used as the primary key of a users table?
note: Directly the db-model-001 scenario, in the asker's own words.

query: isolation levels
note: Deliberately broad: two questions are squarely about isolation levels and MVCC is adjacent. Tests whether a bare topic term retrieves the whole cluster.

query: Detect whether a chain of nodes loops back on itself using constant memory
note: Floyd's algorithm described without naming it, a linked list, or a cycle.

query: Dijkstra negative edge weights
note: Exact terms from dsa-graphs-002; no other bank question mentions Dijkstra.

query: What order should I run jobs in when some of them must finish before others?
note: Topological sort described purely as a scheduling problem.

query: amortised versus worst case cost
note: Two questions are directly about amortised analysis (the complexity question and the doubling array); the two-stack queue uses it as a sub-point.

query: Report the biggest few items out of a huge stream without storing all of it
note: The top-k streaming question, avoiding 'heap', 'top-k' and 'priority queue'.

query: off-by-one errors and the loop invariant in binary search
note: Both binary-search questions are strong lexical matches for 'binary search'; only dsa-bsearch-002 is about invariants and off-by-one.

query: Why does joining text together inside a loop get slower and slower?
note: The immutable-string quadratic-blowup question, phrased as a symptom.

query: separate chaining open addressing load factor
note: Three exact concept keys of dsa-hashing-001.

query: I need to fetch every event between two timestamps efficiently
note: Genuinely spans two domains: dsa-hashing-002 is 'a hash map is the wrong structure for a range scan', db-part-001 is 'partition the events table by time'. Both are defensible answers, which is why this is labelled hard.

query: When is picking the locally best option at each step actually optimal?
note: Greedy-choice correctness without the word 'greedy'. The knapsack question is relevant because it is about where greedy fails.

query: shortest path in an unweighted graph breadth-first search
note: Strong lexical overlap with dsa-graphs-001 and topical overlap with the Dijkstra question.

query: Is a pointer-based collection really faster than a contiguous one for inserts?
note: The array-versus-linked-list tradeoff question, avoiding both structure names.

query: 0/1 knapsack dynamic programming recurrence
note: Exact terms from dsa-dp-001; dsa-dp-002 is the other DP question.

query: How do I stop one client from overwhelming my service with requests?
note: Both rate-limiting questions answer this: one on algorithms, one on rationale and the 429 response.

query: thundering herd
note: Appears only in sys-cache-003's expected_concepts, never in its prose. The case that justified showing the reranker the same document Day 8 indexes.

query: One slow dependency is taking my whole service down with it
note: Cascading failure from a missing timeout; the circuit-breaker question is the adjacent mitigation.

query: The average latency looks healthy but customers keep complaining it is slow
note: Almost the sys-obs-002 scenario; the logs/metrics/traces question is adjacent.

query: CAP theorem during a network partition
note: Exact terms from sys-consist-002 plus a topically close consistency question.

query: What has to change before I can run my API on more than one machine?
note: sys-scale-001 lists exactly this. Vertical-vs-horizontal and sticky sessions are the neighbouring questions.

query: TTL versus write-through versus explicit cache invalidation
note: All three caching questions are strong candidates for a caching query; only sys-cache-001 compares these three strategies. A ranking test.

query: Work that takes minutes should not happen while the caller waits
note: The video-transcoding question, generalised; the queue-semantics question is the follow-on.

query: A retried message charged the customer twice
note: At-least-once delivery and idempotent consumers, stated as the symptom.

query: circuit breaker half-open state
note: Exact terms from sys-ft-002.

query: Where should uploaded files and large binary blobs live?
note: The storage-selection question; 'object storage' is deliberately not used.

query: replication
note: One bare word that is a topic in two different domains: the Postgres read-replica question and the single/multi-leader topology question. Tests whether an ambiguous query retrieves both clusters rather than only one.
